body.heading: String is a ruler
paragraphs: A piece of string can measure anything, even things that bend. Stretch it along the thing you want to measure and pinch where it ends.
Now lay your pinched string next to a ruler or count it in hand spans. You have measured something far bigger than your ruler.

body.heading: Measure the giants
paragraphs: Measure your table. Measure your doorway. Measure your adult lying down — most adults are about one doorway tall.
Write every measurement down with its name: table — 6 hand spans of string. You are building a book of the sizes of your world.

body.heading: Compare two things
paragraphs: Which is longer, the sofa or the rug? String can answer without moving either one.
Long ago, string and rope were real measuring tools. Builders of pyramids used knotted ropes to measure their giant stones.

takeaway: A simple piece of string can measure anything in your home, even things much bigger than a ruler.
materials: A long piece of string or wool
safetyNotes: An adult cuts the string. Never wrap string around anyone's neck — lay it gently alongside for measuring.
screenFreeExtension: Measure the same thing in hand spans and in string lengths and compare the two numbers.
